resources.string: No server set: speed test off
How often NetLogger records one row of radio, GPS and battery values. Applies to the next session; a running session keeps its interval.
Finest detail and more battery use. Android may answer with cached cell data, so some rows repeat the previous values.
Fine enough for drive tests at city speeds, with moderate battery use.
Walks and long static tests; half the rows of 1 s.
Very long sessions with the lowest battery use; too coarse to follow handovers while driving.
Preselected on the Live screen; you can still change it there before you press Start. Stored with each session to tell tests apart.
Whatever you used the last time.
In a car or on a motorbike; speed and handovers matter.
On foot, e.g. around a campus or between indoors and outdoors.
The phone stays at one spot, e.g. a speed test or a long measurement at a fixed place.
Inside a building; GPS may be weak or missing.
NetLogger logs the SIM that carries mobile data when you press Start and stays on it for the whole session. To log another SIM, make it the data SIM in Android\'s SIM settings before you start.
Data SIM now: %1$s (%2$s) in SIM slot %3$s
No data SIM found, or the phone permission is missing.
Start it on the Live screen while a session is logging. It uses mobile data only: turn Wi-Fi off, or the test is refused.

resources.string: Download, then upload: %1$d s each over %2$s, stopped early at %3$d MB down / %4$d MB up.
One test can use up to about %1$d MB of your data plan.
Results are stored in the session with the server URL and the radio values of the same seconds. A test during a traffic capture is flagged, because the capture slows it down.
The main target. Use a server you control, so results stay comparable between tests and days. For a LibreSpeed server, enter its address and tap Fill; any other web server works with three URLs.
Answers small requests quickly, e.g. an empty page.
Serves a large file (tens of MB or more); requested again until the time is up.
Accepts POST requests and throws the data away.
Plain HTTP to %1$s is not allowed in this build, so the test would fail. Use https://, or ask whoever builds the app to allow this host (netlogger.cleartextHosts).
Saved. The Live screen shows \"Run speed test (my server)\" while logging.
No server saved yet: the speed test is off.

Optional, for comparison only. Adds a second button on the Live screen that tests against %1$s. Not your server and never the default: the result depends on Cloudflare\'s nearest site and its route, and many large tests in a row are blocked for a while (HTTP 429). Each result stores the URL it used.
